title: Evals 1:1 action notes — prep + follow-ups
content:
Context / purpose:
- Quick prep for 1:1 with Ethan (focus: recent eval regression on conversational reranker + A/B results for prompt-pruning).
- Use this as my live scratchpad during the call and capture concrete follow-ups.

Agenda (15–20m):
1) 2–3 min: current signal summary (metrics + quick story)
2) 6–8 min: walk through failing prompt sets and example failures
3) 4–6 min: A/B outcome review (control vs candidate, CI, business impact)
4) 3–4 min: decide next experiment steps + owners + timelines

Key numbers to call out (quick hits):
- Prod reranker QPS: ~1.2k (peak) — no capacity spike correlated w/ regression window
- Eval set (week-of-2026-03-22): P@10 dropped from 0.78 -> 0.66 on rerank gold prompts
- A/B traffic sample: 7.5k queries, candidate variant CTR +0.2% (not sig), median latency +12ms
- Prompt-pruning experiment: token reduction ~18% but SAMPLER loss increased slightly (0.03)

Observations / notes to self:
- Regression appears correlated with new prompt normalization rule (trim + collapse whitespace) landed in PR #198.
- Examples show subtle context truncation: model drops important context when prompt tokens compacted into fewer tokens (weird).
- Dev env reproduces fewer failures — suspicious of dataset skew in eval harness vs prod logs.
- A/B shows latency tradeoff good, but quality not uniformly improved across verticals (support vs docs vs chat).

Hypotheses to test (ranked):
H1: Normalization reduces explicit separator tokens, breaking some heuristic prompt quoting -> lower P@10 for reranker. (high priority)
H2: Token compaction interacts with KV-cache alignment in quantized runtime (edge case where attention offset computed differently). (med priority)
H3: Eval set sampling: our eval prompt set overweights short-turn dialogs; change in prompt normalization disproportionately affects long-turn dialogs. (med-low)

Concrete examples to show in 1:1 (bring these):
- Case A: user query about billing — before/after generation with markers showing dropped clause "since last invoice"
- Case B: multi-turn support convo where answer reverts to generic template post-change
- Link to sample JSONL in GH gist: github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/samples/normalize-regression-gist

Immediate asks for Ethan during 1:1:
- Can you confirm whether PR #198 modified any tokenizer rules or just string ops? (quick check)
- Ask infra: any runtime quantization changes bundled with the 2026-03-30 deploy? (if yes, we should coordinate SRE)

Proposed short-term plan (next 7 days):
- A: Rollback normalization on a small canary (5% traffic) for 48h — measure P@10 and sample logs (owner: Priya, due: 2026-04-05).
- B: Run targeted evals comparing full dialogs vs short-turn dialogs (owner: me, Maya; due: 2026-04-04).
- C: Add debug trace to reranker to capture token offsets pre/post-normalization (owner: Zane; due: 2026-04-06).
- D: Quick post-mortem doc stub (start now) capturing timeline + baseline numbers (owner: Maya; due: 2026-04-07).

Longer-term / experiments to queue:
- E: Alternative normalization that preserves separators (A/B with strict vs loose). (owner: eng-experiments; target: next sprint)
- F: Add synthetic evals that stress whitespace-sensitive prompts (small set, integrated into CI).

Follow-ups to assign in meeting (capture owners inline):
- Priya: coordinate canary rollback and capture prod logs (Slack: @priya).
- Zane: add token-offset debug metrics + small dashboard tile in console.
- Ethan: validate PR diff for any tokenizer/byte-level ops and call out if we need to revert.
- Maya (me): run split evals, synth cases, and draft the post-mortem (will ping docs + SRE).

Open questions / unknowns to resolve in 1:1 or afterwards:
- Is the regression confined to a specific model family (gpt-like vs llama family variants)? We need per-model breakdown.
- Are there any retraining or model version swaps coincident with the deploy window? (check model catalog + rollout logs)
- Are analytics filters excluding some user types that would change eval distribution?

Notes for post-meeting commit message / Slack summary (short):
- "Found probable culprit: prompt normalization change (PR #198) — rolling small canary rollback, running targeted evals, adding debug to reranker. Owners: Priya (canary), Zane (debug), Maya (evals/postmortem). Will update by 2026-04-07."

Scratch TODOs (personal, not necessarily assigned):
- grep for "collapse_whitespace" across repo + deploy manifests
- run quick local reproduce with longest-turn examples from support set
- prepare 3 slides for weekly optimize sync (slides: problem, quick data, next steps)

Loose thoughts (brain dump):
- Could leverage Optimize's prefix caching heuristics to detect when normalization compresses meaningful separators and trigger an internal safety rule.
- Possible quick fix: normalization that preserves "\n" as explicit <SEP> token — cheap and reversible.

End-of-doc checklist (mark in meeting):
- [ ] Confirm rollback start time
- [ ] Verify A/B sample sizes for split evals
- [ ] Create postmortem stub and circulate
